title: Pattern matching

outcomes.can: Trace which arm of a switch expression matches a value.
Order property and relational patterns so the specific case wins.
Compute a result for each record type, including zero and negative values.
Repair an arm that can never run and add a missing case.
Apply property patterns to fresh data and keep zero as a real value.

intro: Code often has to ask two questions at once: what kind of value is this, and what is inside it? Pattern matching answers both in one step. This module covers the is test, switch expressions, type patterns and property patterns, using the tracker's updates as data.

steps.title: Test a type and name the result
steps.text: A pattern is a test that a value either matches or does not. The simplest is a type pattern. update is Finished f asks whether update is a Finished record. When it is, f is that same object seen as a Finished, so f.Title is available. A switch expression tries several patterns in order and produces a value. Write the value to test, the word switch, then the arms in braces. Each arm is pattern => result, with a comma between arms. The first arm that matches wins. The discard _ matches anything, so it goes last.

steps.title: Follow two notices
steps.text: Read the method and both calls before running. Choose the two output lines in order.

steps.title: Follow the arms
steps.text: Describe is called twice. new Waiting(0) matches the first arm and returns "Place 0". The arm tests the type, so a Place of 0 is handled like any other number. new Finished("Pack") does not match the first arm, matches the second and returns its Title. The last arm runs only for a Notice type that the arms above do not name. Without it the compiler warns that the switch does not handle every input (CS8509), and a value that matches no arm throws SwitchExpressionException when the program runs.

steps.title: Test what is inside
steps.text: A property pattern tests values inside an object. { Minutes: 0 } matches when the Minutes property equals 0. A relational pattern compares: { Minutes: < 30 } matches any value below 30. One pattern can test several properties, as in { Urgent: true, Minutes: > 60 }. A property pattern can also follow a type, as in Finished { Minutes: 0 } f. Order matters because the first match wins, so put the most specific arm first.

steps.title: Which arm wins?
steps.text: More than one arm can match the same job. Read the arms from the top and predict the first call's result.

steps.title: Read the arms in order
steps.text: Job(0, true) matches the first arm, so it is "empty" even though it is urgent. Job(10, true) is not 0 but is below 30, so it is "short". Job(45, true) fails both Minutes tests and reaches the Urgent arm. Job(45, false) falls through to the discard. If the Urgent arm moved to the top, the first three results would all become "long and urgent".

steps.title: Predict an arm that cannot run
steps.text: This switch has its general arm first. Read the example before checking it.

steps.title: Read the compiler error
steps.text: Check the example. CS8510 says the pattern on line 4 has already been handled by a previous arm. The discard on line 3 matches every number, so the arm below it can never run. C# treats that as an error, not a warning. The fix is to move the general arm below the specific one.

steps.title: Finish two arms
steps.text: The case box above the editor supplies the record types. Change the starter so each update shows its own details.

steps.title: Sort jobs and apply edits
steps.text: Work from each prompt. The first task depends on the order of property patterns. The second computes a number for each record type. Both run against several inputs.

steps.title: Repair the caption
steps.text: Read the compiler error first, then compare the arms with the promised behavior.

questions.prompt: What does the board example print?

choices.feedback: Each arm returns a value built from the record's data, not the name of its type.
The first call matches Waiting, even with a place of 0. The second matches Finished and returns its title.
A place of 0 is still a Waiting record. The type pattern does not look at the number.

questions.prompt: What does Size(new Job(0, true)) return?

choices.feedback: The first arm matches, and no later arm is tried.
The Urgent arm is third. The first arm already matched Minutes: 0.
0 is below 30, but the arm above it matched first.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.feedback: The discard arm comes first, so the < 30 arm could never be reached. The compiler rejects that.
That is what the first arm would return, but the compiler stops before anything runs.

choices.text: The compiler reports an error on line 4.
choices.feedback: Line 3 already matches everything. C# treats an arm that can never run as an error (CS8510).

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter after Exceptions, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every reading is later evidence of ordering patterns. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one pattern form each. They do not check arm order across several record types.
